mainTopic: The end of the story of רבן גמליאל's removal and return, and the הלכות of davening מוסף late and the order of מנחה and מוסף
overview: This amud finishes the famous story of the day רבן גמליאל was removed and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה became head of the ישיבה. A miracle turns his hair white, which explains his words in the משנה, 'I am like a seventy-year-old.' The doors of the בית המדרש open to everyone, מסכת עדיות is taught, and רבן גמליאל still comes to learn. He even takes part in the debate over יהודה גר עמוני, where the ruling follows רבי יהושע. רבן גמליאל then goes to make peace with רבי יהושע, is rebuked for not knowing how poor the scholars are, and is forgiven. The חכמים restore him, and the leadership is shared: three weeks for רבן גמליאל and one for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about מוסף. It rules that מנחה comes before מוסף when both are due, and confirms through רבי זירא that the ruling is רבי יוחנן's. It ends with warnings, based on the פסוק 'נוגי ממועד', against davening מוסף or שחרית past their time according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: His wife's worry and his answer about the expensive cup
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's wife worries that he could be removed just like רבן גמליאל. He answers with a saying about using a fine cup even if it breaks tomorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe they will remove you too. He said to her: Let a person use an expensive cup for one day, even if it breaks tomorrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's wife warns him that taking the job is risky, and he answers her with a folk saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She points out that the same people who removed רבן גמליאל could remove him too. His answer is that an opportunity is worth taking even if it might not last. The honor of leading Torah for one day is worth it.

phrases.english: Perhaps they will remove you.
He said to her:
Let a person use for one day
an expensive cup,
and tomorrow let it break.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא מְעַבְּרִין לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from the previous daf, where רבי אלעזר בן עזריה went to ask his wife before accepting the position.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An honor or opportunity is worth taking even if it may not last.

steps.title: No white hair, and the miracle that fixed it
steps.stepSummary: His wife objects that he is too young-looking to lead. A miracle turns eighteen rows of his hair white.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: You have no white hair. That day he was eighteen years old. A miracle happened for him, and eighteen rows of his hair turned white.
steps.whatsHappening: The wife raises a second worry: he looks too young to be the leader. The גמרא tells us a miracle solved this problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her first worry, about losing the job, was answered by his saying. This second worry, about looking too young to be respected, could not be answered with words, so Heaven answered it with a miracle. He was only eighteen, and eighteen rows of hair turned white.

keyTerms.meaning: white (hair), a sign of age and dignity

phrases.english: She said to him: You have no white hair.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא יוֹמָא בַּר תַּמְנֵי סְרֵי שְׁנֵי הֲוָה,
phrases.english: That day he was eighteen years old;
a miracle happened for him

phrases.aramaic: וְאִהַדַּרוּ לֵיהּ תַּמְנֵי סְרֵי דָּרֵי חִיוָּרָתָא.
phrases.english: and eighteen rows of his hair turned white.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: לֵית לָךָ חִיוָּרָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The wife raises a second concern after her first one was answered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A miracle gave the eighteen-year-old רבי אלעזר בן עזריה the look of an elder.

steps.title: Explaining 'like a seventy-year-old' in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the miracle explains why רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said in the משנה 'I am like a seventy-year-old' and not 'I am seventy.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי אלעזר בן עזריה meant when he said: 'I am like a seventy-year-old,' and not 'I am seventy years old.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the story to a well-known line in the משנה and uses the miracle to explain its exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה he said he was 'like' seventy. That small word now makes sense: he was really eighteen but looked seventy because of the miracle. The story explains the wording, and the wording backs up the story.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what he meant when he said

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was actually seventy. The word 'like' (כְּ) is the whole point: he only looked seventy.

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya meant when he said:
Behold, I am like a seventy-year-old.
And not "seventy years old."

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the miracle about the wording of a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The precise wording 'כְּבֶן שִׁבְעִים' in the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The miracle of the eighteen rows of white hair.

steps.title: The door guard is removed and all students may enter
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that on that day the door guard was removed and every student was allowed in, unlike רבן גמליאל's strict policy.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: On that day they removed the guard at the door, and students were given permission to enter. For רבן גמליאל used to announce: Any student whose inside is not like his outside may not enter the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא describing a big change in the בית המדרש on the day of the switch in leadership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבן גמליאל, only students whose inner character matched their outward behavior were let in, and a guard checked them. On this day that screening ended, and anyone who wanted to learn could come in.

keyTerms.meaning: his inside is like his outside, a sincere person

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole next scene: the flood of new students, and רבן גמליאל's worry that his policy had kept people from Torah.

phrases.english: It was taught: On that day,
they removed the guard at the door
and permission was given to the students to enter.
For Rabban Gamliel used to announce and say:
Any student whose inside is not like his outside,
may not enter the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי אלעזר בן עזריה personally to what changed in the בית המדרש that day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On that day the בית המדרש was opened to all students, ending רבן גמליאל's screening.

steps.title: How many benches were added
steps.stepSummary: Many benches had to be added for the new students. רבי יוחנן reports a disagreement over whether it was 400 or 700.
steps.simpleTranslation: That day many benches were added. רבי יוחנן said: אבא יוסף בן דוסתאי and the רבנן disagree about this. One said 400 benches were added, and one said 700 benches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how many new students came by describing the benches that had to be added, and reports two opinions on the number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is the size of the crowd that had been kept out before. Whether it was 400 or 700 benches, it was a huge increase.

phrases.english: That day, many benches were added.
Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ אַבָּא יוֹסֵף בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי וְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: Abba Yosef ben Dostai and the Rabbis disagree about this.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: אִתּוֹסְפוּ אַרְבַּע מְאָה סַפְסַלֵּי.
phrases.english: One said: Four hundred benches were added.
And one said: Seven hundred benches.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא יוֹמָא אִתּוֹסְפוּ כַּמָּה סַפְסַלֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the result of opening the doors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hundreds of benches (400 or 700) were added for the new students.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's worry and his dream
steps.stepSummary: Seeing all the new students, רבן גמליאל feared he had held back Torah from ישראל. In a dream he was shown white jugs full of ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל became upset. He said: Perhaps, Heaven forbid, I held back Torah from ישראל. They showed him in his dream white jugs filled with ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל feels bad that his strict policy may have kept people from learning, and he is shown a dream that seems to comfort him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The jugs are white on the outside but full of ash inside. That matches his old rule about students whose inside is not like their outside. The dream suggests the students he kept out were not worthy anyway.

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָא חָלְשָׁה דַּעְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel became disheartened,
He said: Perhaps, Heaven forbid,
I held back Torah from Israel.
They showed him in his dream
white jugs filled with ashes.
phrases.notes: White outside, ash inside: a hint at students whose inside doesn't match their outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה קָא חָלְשָׁה דַּעְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבן גמליאל reacts to the crowds described in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל feared he had held back Torah, and a dream seemed to show the excluded students were unworthy.

steps.title: The dream was only to comfort him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the students really were worthless. The dream was shown only to calm רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. That dream was shown to him only to settle his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps in to correct a wrong conclusion someone might draw from the dream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the dream proves the new students were empty inside. The גמרא says no: the students were fine. The dream was a kindness to ease רבן גמליאל's distress, not a true judgment of them.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the dream as proof that the new students were unworthy. The גמרא says the opposite.

phrases.english: But that is not so;
that dream, to settle his mind,
is why they showed it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the natural conclusion from the dream in the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the dream shows the new students were truly unworthy.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dream was meant to comfort, not to give an accurate picture of the students.

steps.title: מסכת עדיות was taught on that day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that מסכת עדיות was taught on that day, and that 'בו ביום' everywhere refers to that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: עדיות was taught on that day. And wherever we say 'on that day,' it means that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that tells us what was learned on that great day, and gives a rule for reading the phrase 'בו ביום.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the doors open and the hall full, a whole מסכת of testimonies about earlier rulings was gathered. Also, whenever a משנה or ברייתא says 'בו ביום,' it is pointing to this same day.

keyTerms.meaning: מסכת עדיות, a collection of testimonies about older rulings

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a key for reading many משניות: 'בו ביום' points to the day רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was appointed.

phrases.english: It was taught: Eduyot was taught on that day.
phrases.notes: This means מסכת עדיות in the משנה.

phrases.english: And anywhere that we say "on that day,"
it was that day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: עֵדֻיוֹת בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם נִשְׁנֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבן גמליאל's feelings to what was learned that day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מסכת עדיות was taught that day, and 'בו ביום' always refers to it.

steps.title: Every open question settled, and רבן גמליאל stayed
steps.stepSummary: Every unresolved הלכה was settled that day, and רבן גמליאל did not stay away from the בית המדרש even for a moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was no הלכה left undecided in the study hall that they did not explain. And even רבן גמליאל did not keep himself away from the study hall, even for one hour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the description of that day: all open questions were resolved, and רבן גמליאל kept learning there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening of the doors brought great Torah results, since nothing was left unclear. רבן גמליאל, even though he had just been removed, still came to learn. He put Torah above his own honor.
steps.whatToRemember: The day רבי אלעזר בן עזריה became leader, the בית המדרש opened to all. Hundreds of benches were added, מסכת עדיות was taught, every open הלכה was settled, and רבן גמליאל still came to learn.

phrases.english: And there was no halacha
that was left hanging in the study hall
that they did not explain.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לֹא מָנַע עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: And even Rabban Gamliel did not hold himself back
from the study hall, even for one hour.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא הָיְתָה הֲלָכָה שֶׁהָיְתָה תְּלוּיָה בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and closes the description of that day.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: That day brought complete clarity in הלכה, and רבן גמליאל kept learning despite being removed.

steps.title: A משנה proves רבן גמליאל was present: an Ammonite convert asks his question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. On 'that day' יהודה, an Ammonite convert, came to the בית המדרש and asked if he may marry into the Jewish people.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: On that day יהודה, an Ammonite convert, came before them in the בית המדרש. He said to them: What is my status regarding entering the congregation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove what it just said: that רבן גמליאל did not stay away from the בית המדרש. This line sets up the story by presenting יהודה's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said רבן גמליאל did not leave the בית המדרש even for a moment. The proof is coming: he takes part in the debate that follows. Here the case is opened. A convert from עמון wants to know if he may marry a Jewish woman.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert who comes from the nation of עמון
To enter the congregation, meaning to marry a born Jew

steps.confusionAlert: 'Entering the congregation' does not mean whether he may convert or come into a shul. It means whether he may marry into the Jewish people.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: On that day
phrases.notes: 'That day' is the day רבן גמליאל was removed and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was appointed.

phrases.english: Yehuda, the Ammonite convert, came
before them in the study hall.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: מָה אֲנִי לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל?
phrases.english: He said to them: What am I regarding entering the congregation?
phrases.notes: He is asking whether he may marry a Jewish woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to back up the claim in step 9 that רבן גמליאל stayed in the בית המדרש.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן גמליאל did not stay away from the בית המדרש on that day
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in ידים 4:4 about יהודה גר עמוני

steps.title: Two opposite rulings: forbidden or permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל rules that the convert may not marry into ישראל. רבי יהושע rules that he may.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to him: You are forbidden to enter the congregation. רבי יהושע said to him: You are permitted to enter the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: Two great חכמים give opposite answers to יהודה's question. This sets up the debate that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice that רבן גמליאל is the one speaking first. This is exactly the proof that he was in the בית המדרש that day. Each side will now defend his position with פסוקים.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to him:
You are forbidden to enter the congregation.
Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
You are permitted to enter the congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: אָסוּר אַתָּה לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two answers to the question asked in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל: forbidden. רבי יהושע: permitted.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל cites the Torah's ban on Ammonites
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל challenges רבי יהושע with the פסוק that says an Ammonite may not enter the congregation of ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to him: Doesn't the Torah already say, 'An Ammonite and a Moabite shall not enter the congregation of ה׳'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל attacks רבי יהושע's ruling with a clear פסוק. The Torah openly forbids Ammonites.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to settle the question. This man is from עמון, and the Torah says Ammonites may never marry into ישראל. So how can רבי יהושע permit him?

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it already stated? This is a way of challenging someone with a פסוק.
A Moabite, someone from the nation of מואב
The congregation of ה׳, meaning the Jewish people for marriage

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to him:
phrases.notes: Now he is speaking to רבי יהושע, not to the convert.

phrases.english: But wasn't it already stated:
"An Ammonite and a Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord"?
phrases.notes: דברים 23:4

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר ״לֹא יָבֹא עַמּוֹנִי וּמוֹאָבִי בִּקְהַל ה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהושע's permissive ruling from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's ruling that the Ammonite convert is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah clearly forbids Ammonites from entering the congregation, and this man is from עמון.

steps.title: סנחריב mixed up the nations, so he is probably not a real Ammonite
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers that סנחריב moved all the nations around. So the people living in עמון today are mostly not real Ammonites. Anyone who comes from a mixed group is treated as part of the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: Do עמון and מואב still live in their own place? סנחריב king of אשור already came up and mixed up all the nations, as it says: 'I have removed the borders of peoples, and robbed their treasures, and brought down the inhabitants like a mighty one.' And whoever separates from a group is assumed to come from the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע defends his ruling. He agrees with the פסוק, but he argues that this man is probably not a true Ammonite at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's ban is still fully in force. It only applies to someone who is really from the nation of עמון. Since סנחריב scattered the nations, most people today are not real Ammonites. The rule כל דפריש מרובא פריש lets us treat this convert as coming from that permitted majority.

keyTerms.meaning: The king of אשור who exiled and resettled many nations
Whatever separates from a group is assumed to come from its majority

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע does not argue with the Torah's ban on Ammonites. He argues that we cannot know this man is really an Ammonite, so we follow the majority.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע is not saying the law of עמוני no longer applies. The law still stands. The question is only whether this person truly belongs to that nation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the idea that once nations were mixed up, the identity-based bans on certain nations can no longer be applied.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב בִּמְקוֹמָן הֵן יוֹשְׁבִין?
phrases.english: Do Ammon and Moab reside in their own place?
Sennacherib, king of Assyria, already came up
and scrambled all the nations,
phrases.notes: He moved whole peoples out of their lands and settled other peoples in their place.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "I have removed the borders of the peoples,
and have robbed their treasures,
and have brought down as a mighty one the inhabitants,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 10:13

phrases.english: And anything that separates, separates from the majority.
phrases.notes: Since most people around are not real Ammonites, we assume this convert isn't one either.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב בִּמְקוֹמָן הֵן יוֹשְׁבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבן גמליאל's challenge from the פסוק in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: the פסוק applies only to real Ammonites, and this man is presumed not to be one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone from the land of עמון is an Ammonite and is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because סנחריב mixed up the nations, the convert is presumed to come from the permitted majority.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: the Ammonites already returned to their land
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל cites a נבואה that ה׳ would bring back the people of עמון. He says this already happened, so real Ammonites live there again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to him: But doesn't it already say, 'And afterward I will bring back the captivity of the children of עמון, says ה׳'? And they have already returned!
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל pushes back against רבי יהושע's answer. He says the Ammonites were brought back home, so the mixing no longer matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע's answer depended on the Ammonites still being scattered. רבן גמליאל uses a פסוק from ירמיהו to say they came back. If so, the people in עמון are real Ammonites again, and the ban applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Captivity, or the exiles who are brought back

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to him:
But wasn't it already stated:
"But afterward I will bring back the captivity
of the children of Ammon, says the Lord,"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 49:6

phrases.english: and they have already returned!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר ״וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן אָשִׁיב אֶת שְׁבוּת בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן נְאֻם ה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 13 by claiming the scattering was undone.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's claim that the Ammonites are still mixed among the nations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A נבואה promised the Ammonites would return home, and רבן גמליאל assumes it already came true.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: a promise of return doesn't mean it already happened
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers that ה׳ also promised to bring back ישראל, and that has not happened yet. So we cannot assume עמון has returned either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: But doesn't it also say, 'And I will return the captivity of My people ישראל'? And they have not yet returned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע knocks down רבן גמליאל's proof. A נבואה about returning does not show that the return already took place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל assumed the promise to עמון was already fulfilled. רבי יהושע shows that a similar promise to ישראל is still waiting to come true. So the return of עמון is not proven, and the mixed-up situation from סנחריב still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And still not, or not yet

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
But wasn't it already stated:
"And I will return the captivity of My people Israel,"
phrases.notes: עמוס 9:14

phrases.english: and they have not yet returned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר ״וְשַׁבְתִּי אֶת שְׁבוּת עַמִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 by showing its proof does not hold.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the proof: a promised return is not proof that the return already happened.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The נבואה about עמון shows they already returned home.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like the promise to ישראל, the promise to עמון may still be in the future, so the nations are still mixed.

steps.title: The convert is permitted right away
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים immediately ruled like רבי יהושע and allowed יהודה to marry into ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately they permitted him to enter the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The debate ends. The בית המדרש rules like רבי יהושע and permits the Ammonite convert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע: since the nations are mixed, an Ammonite convert today may marry into ישראל. For our גמרא, the main point is that רבן גמליאל was part of this debate. That proves he did not stay away from the בית המדרש that day, as step 9 said.
steps.whatToRemember: The story of יהודה גר עמוני serves two purposes. It teaches the הלכה that today's Ammonite convert is permitted. It also proves that רבן גמליאל stayed and took part in the learning on the day he was removed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is why converts from these nations are accepted for marriage today, since the original nations can no longer be identified.

phrases.english: Immediately they permitted him to enter the congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד הִתִּירוּהוּ לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the debate in favor of רבי יהושע after his answer in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The Ammonite convert is permitted, and רבן גמליאל's part in the debate proves he was in the בית המדרש that day.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל goes to appease רבי יהושע and sees his blackened walls
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל sees that the people side with רבי יהושע and decides to go and appease him. At his house he sees black walls and realizes רבי יהושע works with charcoal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said: Since this is how things are, I will go and make peace with רבי יהושע. When he got to his house, he saw that the walls were black. He said to him: From the walls of your house I can tell that you work with charcoal.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves on from the debate. רבן גמליאל goes to apologize to רבי יהושע and is surprised by what he sees at his house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in Step 16 showed רבן גמליאל that the חכמים were following רבי יהושע. So he decides to go and make peace. His remark about the black walls shows he never knew how hard רבי יהושע had to work to earn a living. That sets up the rebuke in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Since this is how it is
I will appease him, make peace with him
Someone who works with charcoal or coal

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said:
Since this is how it is,
phrases.notes: He means that everyone just ruled like רבי יהושע, as we saw in Step 16.

phrases.english: I will go and appease Rabbi Yehoshua.
When he reached his house,
he saw that the walls of his house were black.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִכּוֹתְלֵי בֵיתְךָ אַתָּה נִיכָּר
phrases.english: He said to him: From the walls of your house it can be seen
that you are a charcoal worker.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: הוֹאִיל וְהָכִי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the ruling in Step 16. Now that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע, רבן גמליאל seeks to make peace.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל chooses to go and make peace with רבי יהושע, and learns that רבי יהושע supports himself with hard physical work.

steps.title: רבי יהושע rebukes רבן גמליאל for not knowing how the scholars suffer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers sharply: woe to a generation whose leader does not know how hard תלמידי חכמים struggle to earn a living and feed themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: Woe to the generation that has you as its leader, because you do not know how much תלמידי חכמים suffer, how they earn a living and how they get food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers רבן גמליאל's remark with a rebuke. He says a real leader should know how poor the scholars are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל's surprise showed he had no idea of the scholars' hardship. רבי יהושע turns that surprise into a criticism of how he has been leading. This is why the apology in the next step is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Its leader, the one who looks after it

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אוֹי לוֹ לַדּוֹר שֶׁאַתָּה פַּרְנָסוֹ,
phrases.english: He said to him: Woe to the generation that you are its leader,
since you do not know
the hardship of Torah scholars,
how they earn a living
and how they feed themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אוֹי לוֹ לַדּוֹר שֶׁאַתָּה פַּרְנָסוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבן גמליאל's comment about the blackened walls.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A leader must know what the scholars of his generation are going through.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל asks forgiveness and רבי יהושע is appeased
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל apologizes. רבי יהושע ignores him at first, but when רבן גמליאל asks in the honor of his father, רבי יהושע forgives him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to him: I wronged you, forgive me. רבי יהושע paid no attention to him. He asked again: Do it for the honor of my father. Then רבי יהושע was appeased.
steps.whatsHappening: This step settles the personal fight between the two. The first apology is ignored, and the second one, made in the honor of רבן גמליאל's father, works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An apology alone was not enough for רבי יהושע. רבן גמליאל then appeals to the honor of his father's family, and רבי יהושע gives in. Now the way is open to return רבן גמליאל to his position.

keyTerms.meaning: I wronged you, I insulted you
He paid no attention to him

steps.whatToRemember: The personal fight is over: רבי יהושע forgave רבן גמליאל because of the honor of his father.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: נַעֲנֵיתִי לְךָ מְחוֹל לִי.
phrases.english: He said to him: I have wronged you, forgive me.
He paid no attention to him.
Do it for the honor of my father.
phrases.notes: This is רבן גמליאל speaking again, making a second request. The גמרא doesn't say 'he said' here.

phrases.english: He was appeased.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: נַעֲנֵיתִי לְךָ מְחוֹל לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבן גמליאל responds to the rebuke with an apology, and the apology is finally accepted.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהושע forgives רבן גמליאל, which opens the way to give him back his position.

steps.title: Who will tell the Sages, and a launderer volunteers
steps.stepSummary: The people ask who will go tell the חכמים that the two have made peace. A certain launderer offers to go.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Who will go and tell the חכמים? A certain launderer said to them: I will go.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. Someone needs to bring the news to the בית המדרש, and a simple launderer agrees to bring it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new peace has to reach the חכמים in the בית המדרש. Only a launderer offers to go, not one of the scholars. This prepares the message that comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A launderer, someone who washes clothes

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ: מַאן נֵיזִיל וְלֵימָא לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: They said: Who will go and tell the Sages?
A certain launderer said to them:
I will go.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ: מַאן נֵיזִיל וְלֵימָא לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the peace is made, the question is how to tell the חכמים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who will bring the news of the peace to the חכמים?

steps.title: רבי יהושע's message: the one who wears the garment should keep wearing it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע sends a parable to the בית המדרש. The one who wore the garment, רבן גמליאל, should wear it again. The one who never wore it should not tell him to take it off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע sent a message to the בית המדרש: The one who wears the garment should wear the garment. Should the one who does not wear the garment say to the one who wears it, 'Take off your garment and I will wear it'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע sends a message, carried by the launderer, saying that רבן גמליאל should be given back his position as נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'garment' stands for the position of נשיא. רבן גמליאל had it first, so it belongs to him. It is not right for someone new to take it away from him, so he should be returned to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall, the בית המדרש

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לְהוּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua sent a message to them at the study hall:
The one who wears the garment should wear the garment,
phrases.notes: The garment is a picture for the position of נשיא, which רבן גמליאל used to hold.

phrases.english: and the one who does not wear the garment,
should he say to the one who wears the garment:
Take off your garment and I will wear it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לְהוּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the message the launderer volunteered to carry.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל, the original נשיא, should be given back his position.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא locks the gates against the message
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא tells the חכמים to lock the gates. He thinks the messenger is one of רבן גמליאל's servants who has come to bother them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to the חכמים: Lock the gates, so that the servants of רבן גמליאל will not come and bother the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The message is pushed away. רבי עקיבא does not believe it really comes from רבי יהושע, so he shuts the doors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא sees the messenger as a servant of רבן גמליאל, not as someone sent by רבי יהושע. So the message does not work. This makes רבי יהושע come in person in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to the Sages:
Lock the gates
so that the servants of Rabban Gamliel will not come
phrases.notes: He seems to think the launderer was really sent by רבן גמליאל and not by רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: and bother the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבָּנַן: טְרוּקוּ גַּלֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא refuses to accept the message from Step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The message sent through the launderer is not accepted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי עקיבא does not trust the messenger. He thinks he comes from רבן גמליאל's side.

steps.title: רבי יהושע comes himself with the parable of the one who sprinkles
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע decides to go himself. He knocks on the door and gives a second parable: a sprinkler who is the son of a sprinkler should go on sprinkling, and an outsider should not call his water and ashes worthless.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: It is better that I get up and go to them myself. He came and knocked on the door. He said to them: A sprinkler son of a sprinkler should sprinkle. Should one who is not a sprinkler and not the son of a sprinkler say to a sprinkler son of a sprinkler, 'Your water is just cave water and your ashes are just ashes from a fire'?!
steps.whatsHappening: Since the message did not work, רבי יהושע comes in person. He gives the same idea again with a new parable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new parable adds family line: רבן גמליאל comes from a family of leaders, like a person who sprinkles the purifying water and whose father sprinkled before him. An outsider has no right to call his service worthless. Coming in person shows the חכמים that the message really comes from רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sprinkles the purifying water
Cave water, plain water that cannot purify

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
It is better that I get up and go to them myself.
He came and knocked on the door.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: מַזֶּה בֶּן מַזֶּה יַזֶּה.
phrases.english: He said to them: A sprinkler son of a sprinkler should sprinkle.
phrases.notes: A מזה sprinkles the water mixed with פרה אדומה ashes to make people טהור. Here it stands for רבן גמליאל.

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא מַזֶּה וְלֹא בֶּן מַזֶּה
phrases.english: And should one who is neither a sprinkler nor the son of a sprinkler
say to a sprinkler son of a sprinkler:
Your water is cave water
and your ashes are ashes from a fire?!
phrases.notes: In other words, 'your water and ashes are plain and worthless,' which would mean the sprinkling doesn't work.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: מוּטָב דְּאֵיקוּם וְאֵיזִיל אֲנָא לְגַבַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the locked gates of Step 22. רבי יהושע comes in person and gives his message again.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who comes from a line of leaders, like רבן גמליאל, should keep his role, and an outsider should not push him out.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא agrees to go to רבן גמליאל the next morning
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא asks רבי יהושע if he really forgave. He explains that everything the חכמים did was for רבי יהושע's honor, and says the two of them will go to רבן גמליאל's door early the next morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: רבי יהושע, have you been appeased? Everything we did was only for your honor. Tomorrow morning, you and I will go early to his door.
steps.whatsHappening: This ends this part of the story. Once רבי עקיבא hears it from רבי יהושע himself, he agrees to work toward giving רבן גמליאל back his position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא explains that the חכמים removed רבן גמליאל only to defend רבי יהושע's honor. Now that רבי יהושע has forgiven him, there is no reason to keep רבן גמליאל out. So they plan to go to him the next day.

keyTerms.meaning: We will go early in the morning

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים acted only to protect רבי יהושע's honor. Once he forgave רבן גמליאל, they were ready to bring רבן גמליאל back.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
Rabbi Yehoshua, have you been appeased?
Did we do anything except for your honor?
Tomorrow, you and I will go early to his doorway.
phrases.notes: 'His' means רבן גמליאל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, נִתְפַּיַּיסְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא answers רבי יהושע's personal appeal and accepts it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Once רבי יהושע has forgiven him, the חכמים agree to begin bringing רבן גמליאל back, and רבי עקיבא and רבי יהושע plan to go to him the next morning.

steps.title: What should be done with the new leader?
steps.stepSummary: Now that רבן גמליאל is coming back, the חכמים ask what to do about רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: What shall we do?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask a practical question: what happens to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה now that רבן גמליאל is returning? This line sets up the options the גמרא will test next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now two people with a claim to lead the ישיבה. The next steps try out possible solutions one at a time.

phrases.english: They said: What shall we do?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הֵיכִי נַעֲבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the plan to go back to רבן גמליאל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to handle two leaders at the same time.

steps.title: He cannot be removed
steps.stepSummary: Removing רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is rejected, because a person raised to a holy position is never lowered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we remove him? We have a tradition: we raise people up in holiness, and we do not bring them down.
steps.whatsHappening: The first idea is to simply remove רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. The גמרא rejects it right away using a known rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule מעלין בקדש ואין מורידין means that someone who has been given a holy role keeps it. Since רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was made head, he cannot be demoted.

keyTerms.meaning: We raise up in holiness and do not bring down

steps.whyThisMatters: מעלין בקדש ואין מורידין is a basic principle that comes up all over ש״ס.

phrases.english: Shall we remove him?
We have learned: we raise up in holiness
and we do not bring down.

steps.triggerLanguage: נַעְבְּרֵיהּ — גְּמִירִי מַעֲלִין בַּקֹּדֶשׁ וְאֵין מוֹרִידִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first answer to the question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The option of removing רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It goes against מעלין בקדש ואין מורידין.

steps.title: Taking equal turns would cause jealousy
steps.stepSummary: Having the two leaders take turns week by week is rejected, because it would lead to jealousy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let one teach one week and the other teach one week? That would lead to jealousy.
steps.whatsHappening: A second idea is tried: an equal split, one week each. The גמרא rejects this one too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a fully equal split, no one is clearly in charge, and that leads to rivalry. So the plan has to keep רבן גמליאל on top while still giving רבי אלעזר בן עזריה a real role.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him teach / give the דרשה

phrases.english: Let one master teach one week
and the other master one week?
They will come to be jealous.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִדְרוֹשׁ מָר חֲדָא שַׁבְּתָא וּמַר חֲדָא שַׁבְּתָא — אָתֵי לְקַנּאוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a second option and rejects it.

steps.title: Three weeks and one week
steps.stepSummary: The final plan: רבן גמליאל teaches three weeks, and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה teaches one week.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבן גמליאל will teach three weeks, and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה will teach one week.
steps.whatsHappening: The word אלא marks the plan that works. רבן גמליאל gets most of the weeks, and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה keeps one week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This plan solves both problems. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is not demoted completely, so מעלין בקדש is kept, and רבן גמליאל is clearly the main leader, so there is no reason for jealousy.

phrases.english: Rather: let רבן גמליאל teach
three weeks

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה חֲדָא שַׁבְּתָא.
phrases.english: and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה one week.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לִדְרוֹשׁ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל תְּלָתָא שַׁבָּתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the question after both earlier options were rejected.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The leadership is shared 3:1, with רבן גמליאל as the main leader.

steps.title: This explains a line in חגיגה
steps.stepSummary: The three-and-one plan explains a ברייתא that asks whose week it was.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what the master meant: Whose week was it? It was the week of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that this story explains a line in another ברייתא. That line only makes sense if there were set turns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question "whose week was it?" assumes that leaders took turns by the week. The arrangement described here is the background to that line.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what the master said

phrases.english: And this is what the master said:
Whose week was it?
phrases.notes: This line is quoted from a ברייתא in מסכת חגיגה.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה הָיְתָה.
phrases.english: It was רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the plan to another source.
steps.raayaObject: That the leaders took turns by the week.

steps.title: Who the student was
steps.stepSummary: The student who started the whole story was רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that student was רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The story closes by naming the student whose question about ערבית started the whole episode.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new about the law is added here. It is a closing detail that finishes the story.
steps.whatToRemember: The story ends with shared leadership: רבן גמליאל teaches three weeks and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה teaches one. The student who asked was רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.

phrases.english: And that student
phrases.notes: This is the student who asked whether תפלת ערבית is a רשות, at the very start of the story.

phrases.english: was רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final detail of the story.

steps.title: Davening מוסף late
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה: מוסף may be davened all day, but רבי יוחנן says someone who pushes it off too long is called a פושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And מוסף may be said all day." רבי יוחנן said: And he is called negligent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which says מוסף can be davened all day. רבי יוחנן adds that someone who delays it too much is called a פושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תפלה still counts, so after the deadline it is valid, not lost. But putting it off that long is still treated as wrong.
steps.confusionAlert: פושע does not mean the תפלה is invalid. He did fulfill his obligation; he is only criticized for the delay.

phrases.english: "And of מוסף, all day."
רבי יוחנן said: And he is called "negligent."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁל מוּסָפִין כׇּל הַיּוֹם. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story is over, and the גמרא returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מוסף said late is valid, but the person is called a פושע.

steps.title: מנחה first, because it is more frequent
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: if both מנחה and מוסף are due, he davens מנחה first, because it is more frequent.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he has two תפלות to daven, מנחה and מוסף, he davens מנחה first and then מוסף, because this one is frequent and that one is not.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא raises the case where someone has to daven both מנחה and מוסף. The first opinion says מנחה comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is the rule of תדיר: something that comes more often goes first. מנחה is said every day, while מוסף is only said on special days.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי תְּפִלּוֹת,
phrases.english: The רבנן taught: If there were two tefillos before him,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל מִנְחָה וְאַחַת שֶׁל מוּסָף —
phrases.english: one of מנחה and one of מוסף,
he davens מנחה
and afterwards he davens מוסף,
because this one is frequent, and that one is not frequent.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי תְּפִלּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the time limits of מוסף.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: מוסף first, because its time is running out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says to daven מוסף first, because its time is ending soon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He davens מוסף and then מנחה, because this מצוה is passing and that one is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion and puts מוסף first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is a different factor: a מצוה whose time is about to end comes first. מוסף's time ends soon, while there is still plenty of time for מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה whose time is running out

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁל מוּסָף
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: He davens מוסף
and afterwards he davens מנחה,
because this is a מצוה that is passing,
and that is a מצוה that is not passing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing view in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מוסף first, because its time is running out.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's ruling: מנחה first
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה is to daven מנחה first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה is that he davens מנחה and afterwards מוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן decides the מחלוקת in favor of the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case, the frequency of מנחה (תדיר) counts for more than the urgency of מוסף's deadline.

keyTerms.meaning: The ruling we follow in practice

steps.whatToRemember: When both are due: מנחה first, then מוסף. רבי יוחנן rules like the תנא קמא and not like רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה is
he davens מנחה
and afterwards he davens מוסף.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the מחלוקת.

steps.title: רבי זירא sits at the doorway
steps.stepSummary: When רבי זירא got tired from learning, he sat at the door of the בית מדרש so he could stand up for the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא was tired from learning, he would go sit at the doorway of רבי נתן בר טובי's house of study. He said: When the חכמים pass by, I will stand up for them and get reward.
steps.whatsHappening: A short story begins. This line sets the scene for the exchange about the הלכה that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even while resting, רבי זירא found a way to earn a מצוה: standing up to honor תלמידי חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי זֵירָא כִּי הֲוָה חֲלִישׁ מִגִּירְסֵיהּ
phrases.english: רבי זירא, when he was weary from his learning,
would go and sit

phrases.aramaic: אַפִּתְחָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי נָתָן בַּר טוֹבִי.
phrases.english: at the doorway of רבי נתן בר טובי's house of study.
He said: When the חכמים pass by,
I will stand up before them
and receive reward.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא כִּי הֲוָה חֲלִישׁ מִגִּירְסֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that will confirm רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene for the story.

steps.title: Who said a הלכה inside?
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן בר טובי comes out, and רבי זירא asks him who said a הלכה in the בית מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן בר טובי came out. He said to him: Who said a הלכה in the בית מדרש?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks what הלכה was just said inside. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי זירא was sitting outside, he wants to hear what he missed.

phrases.aramaic: נְפַק אֲתָא רַבִּי נָתָן בַּר טוֹבִי,
phrases.english: רבי נתן בר טובי came out.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאן אֲמַר הֲלָכָה בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Who said a הלכה in the house of study?
phrases.notes: Here it is רבי זירא asking רבי נתן בר טובי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאן אֲמַר הֲלָכָה בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which הלכה was said, and by whom.

steps.title: Not like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן said the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה, who puts מוסף before מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה is not like רבי יהודה, who said a person davens מוסף and afterwards מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן בר טובי answers by reporting רבי יוחנן's ruling, and it backs up step 34.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same ruling is said in a new way: "not like רבי יהודה" instead of "מנחה first." Either way, the outcome is the same.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said:
The הלכה is not like רבי יהודה
who said a person davens מוסף
and afterwards davens מנחה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן ruled against רבי יהודה, so מנחה comes first.

steps.title: Did רבי יוחנן really say it?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רבי נתן בר טובי whether רבי יוחנן himself said this הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: Did רבי יוחנן say it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks to confirm who said the ruling he just heard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 37, רבי נתן reported that the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה. Now רבי זירא wants to be sure the ruling truly comes from רבי יוחנן, because it matters who said a הלכה.

phrases.english: He said to him: Did רבי יוחנן say it?
phrases.notes: רבי זירא is asking about the ruling from step 37, that מנחה comes before מוסף.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַמְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבי נתן's report by checking its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ruling truly came from רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Yes, learned forty times
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן confirms that רבי יוחנן said it. רבי זירא reviewed it from רבי נתן forty times.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. He reviewed it from him forty times.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן answers yes. Then the גמרא adds that רבי זירא reviewed this teaching from רבי נתן forty times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן is not unsure about the source: רבי יוחנן said it. רבי זירא then went over the ruling with רבי נתן forty times. That repeated review leads to the question in the next step, why this ruling is so precious to him.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.
He learned it from him forty times.
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי זירא: he reviewed this teaching from רבי נתן forty times.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, רבי יוחנן said it. רבי זירא reviewed it from רבי נתן forty times.

steps.title: Is it your only one, or a new one?
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן asks רבי זירא why this ruling is so precious to him: is it the only one he has, or is it new to him?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is it a single one for you, or is it a new one for you?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן sees how eager רבי זירא is to confirm this teaching and asks why it means so much to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gives two possibilities: maybe this is the only הלכה רבי זירא has from רבי יוחנן, or maybe this ruling is something he never heard before. The question sets up רבי זירא's explanation.

phrases.english: He said to him: Is it a single one for you,
phrases.notes: He means: is this the only teaching of רבי יוחנן you have?

phrases.english: or is it a new one for you?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲדָא הִיא לָךְ, אוֹ חֲדַת הִיא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the questioning around, asking why רבי זירא cares so much.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ruling is so important to רבי זירא.

steps.title: New, because of a doubt about רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the ruling is new to him, because he was unsure whether it came from רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is new for me, because I was in doubt about רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains that he had a doubt about who said this, and now it is cleared up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He had heard the idea before, but was not sure if it was in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי. Now he knows it was רבי יוחנן, so in that sense it is 'new.' This mention of רבי יהושע בן לוי leads into the next statement.
steps.whatToRemember: The ruling that מנחה comes before מוסף is clearly from רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is new for me,
because I was in doubt
about רבי יהושע בן לוי.
phrases.notes: He wasn't sure whether the ruling was said by רבי יהושע בן לוי or by רבי יוחנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲדַת הִיא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי נתן's question and ends the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is new, because he had been unsure if it was said by רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: Late מוסף and the פסוק of נוגי ממועד
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says that one who davens מוסף after seven hours, according to רבי יהודה, fits the פסוק 'נוגי ממועד.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Anyone who davens מוסף after seven hours, according to רבי יהודה, about him the פסוק says: 'Those who are נוגי far from the appointed time, I gathered from you.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: davening מוסף too late is criticized with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the time for מוסף ends after seven hours. Davening after that is compared to the people in the פסוק who pushed off the times of the festivals. The גמרא will next explain what נוגי means.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who are נוגי far from the appointed time

phrases.english: רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
Anyone who davens the מוסף prayer
after seven hours, according to רבי יהודה,
about him the פסוק says:
"Those who are נוגי far from the appointed time, I gathered from you, they were."
phrases.notes: צפניה 3:18

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל תְּפִלָּה שֶׁל מוּסָפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mention of רבי יהושע בן לוי leads into one of his teachings about the time of מוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Davening מוסף after seven hours (for רבי יהודה) is criticized by the פסוק נוגי ממועד.

steps.title: How do we know נוגי means destruction?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the word נוגי means breaking or destruction.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that this word נוגי is a word for destruction?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of the meaning of נוגי in רבי יהושע בן לוי's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning only works if נוגי means something bad like destruction. So the גמרא wants a source showing that meaning.

phrases.english: How is it implied that this word נוגי
is a word for destruction?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי נוּגֵי לִישָּׁנָא דִתְבָרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of the word meaning used in step 42.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that נוגי means destruction.

steps.title: רב יוסף's תרגום
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's Aramaic translation of the פסוק says destruction comes on those who delayed the festival times in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף translates: Destruction comes upon the enemies of the house of Israel, because they delayed the times of the festivals in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רב יוסף's Aramaic translation of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף translates נוגי as 'destruction' and explains it is because they delayed the festival times. This proves both the meaning of the word and the connection to doing things late.

phrases.english: As רב יוסף translates:

phrases.aramaic: תְּבָרָא אָתֵי עַל שָׂנְאֵיהוֹן דְּבֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: Destruction comes upon the enemies of the house of Israel,
phrases.notes: "Enemies of Israel" is a polite way of saying Israel itself, so as not to speak badly of them directly.

phrases.english: because they delayed the times of the festivals in ירושלים.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִמְתַרְגֵּם רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the meaning of נוגי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף's תרגום renders נוגי as destruction for delaying the festival times.

steps.title: Late שחרית and the same פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that one who davens שחרית after four hours, according to רבי יהודה, fits the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Anyone who davens שחרית after four hours, according to רבי יהודה, about him the פסוק says: 'Those who are נוגי far from the appointed time, I gathered from you.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second, similar statement: this time about davening שחרית too late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, שחרית may be davened until four hours. רבי אלעזר applies the same פסוק to someone who davens after that, but as we will see, he reads נוגי differently.

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said:
Anyone who davens the שחרית prayer
after four hours, according to רבי יהודה,
about him the פסוק says:
"Those who are נוגי far from the appointed time, I gathered from you, they were."

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Davening שחרית after four hours (for רבי יהודה) is criticized by the פסוק נוגי ממועד.

steps.title: How do we know נוגי means sorrow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that in רבי אלעזר's reading נוגי means pain or sorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that this word נוגי is a word for pain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for רבי אלעזר's meaning of נוגי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here נוגי is understood as sorrow, not destruction. So the גמרא needs a different proof than רב יוסף's תרגום.

phrases.english: How is it implied that this word נוגי
is a word for pain?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of the word meaning used in step 45.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that נוגי means sorrow.

steps.title: Proof from תהלים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the meaning from the פסוק 'My soul drips from sorrow (תוגה).'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'My soul drips from sorrow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק where the same root means sorrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תוגה shares a root with נוגי and clearly means sorrow. That shows נוגי can mean pain.

phrases.english: As it is written: "My soul drips from sorrow."
phrases.notes: תהלים 119:28

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: דָּלְפָה נַפְשִׁי מִתּוּגָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the meaning of נוגי as sorrow.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word תוגה in תהלים means sorrow, so נוגי does too.

steps.title: Another proof from איכה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a different פסוק showing that נוגי means sorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: From here: 'Her maidens are sorrowful (נוגות), and she is bitter.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives another source for the same meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His פסוק uses נוגות, which is even closer in form to נוגי, next to the word 'bitter.' That makes the meaning of sorrow very clear.
steps.whatToRemember: Two warnings use the פסוק נוגי ממועד against davening late according to רבי יהודה: מוסף after seven hours, and שחרית after four hours.
